comparisons.peer_topic: R&D Expense Increase and AI Headcount
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's research and development expenses increased by 10% to $6.5 billion in 2024, primarily driven by higher employee-related costs resulting from an increase in headcount to support the company's AI strategy.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD reported increases in operating expenses for fiscal year 2024 driven by employee growth and compensation. NVDA explicitly stated that operating expenses increased due to 'growth in employees and compensation increases' (nvda_2024_7_P024_S001). Similarly, AMD reported that its Research and Development expenses increased by 10% to $6.5 billion, attributing the rise primarily to 'higher employee-related costs due to an increase in headcount in support of our AI strategy' (amd_2024_7_P045_S001 and amd_2024_7_P045_S002). While NVDA presents a broader operating expense trend, AMD's specific R&D expense disclosure mirrors the underlying driver of personnel cost expansion cited by NVDA.

sentences.text: Operating expenses increased for fiscal year 2024, driven by growth in employees and compensation increases.
Research and development expenses of $6.5 billion in 2024 increased by $584 million, or 10%, compared to $5.9 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily due to higher employee-related costs due to an increase in headcount in support of our AI strategy.
